title: Fallen man wholly infected outside grace
source_text: V. Quippe homo sibi relictus, & extra Dei gratiam, totus peccato infectus est, & a Deo aversus: facultates ejus omnes in malum pronae, & imago illa Dei primitus homini impressa, originali labe, quam a primo nostro parente contraximus, miseran-dum in modum foedata & dissipata est. Nam inde caligo summa mentem hominis occupavit, & voluntatem perversitas, & in affectibus maxima perturbatio coorta est, adeo ut homo carnalis, & nondum per gratiam a servitute peccati redemptus, Dei sit inimicus, nec se divinae legi subjiciat; imo nequidem id facere possit, ut docet Apostolus Rom. 8. vers. 8.
pass_a_gloss: For man left to himself and outside God's grace is wholly infected with sin and turned away from God: all his faculties are prone to evil, and that image of God originally impressed on man is miserably stained and shattered by the original blot which we contracted from our first parent. From this a deep darkness has occupied the mind, perversity the will, and a great disturbance has arisen in the affections, so that the fleshly man, not yet redeemed by grace from sin's slavery, is God's enemy and does not subject himself to the divine law—indeed cannot even do so, as the Apostle teaches in Romans 8:8.
pass_b_english: Outside grace man is wholly sin-infected, averted from God, faculties prone to evil.
Original stain darkens mind, warps will, disorders affections—Rom 8:8: the fleshly cannot please God.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1039.
